sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
La Rochelle has been restricting cars in its centre for a decade. The Vieux-Port quay was closed to cars in July 2015 and became pedestrian and cycle-only, after the deputy mayor said 9,000 vehicles a day used it, 6,000 of them only passing through [0]. In 2016 the city lowered car park tariffs and raised on-street ones so that on-street parking was dearer than the car parks, steering visitors to car parks and commuters to park-and-ride sites [1]. In July 2023 it made permanent a pedestrianisation trial around the market, with retractable bollards raised day and night and authorised users let in [5]. An agglomeration study of a low-emission zone began in March 2022, and that is all we found on a zone [2].

Street parking was reformed on 2 January 2024. Two zones were set up: an orange hyper-centre of 21 streets and squares, at €1 per 15 minutes with a two-hour maximum, and a larger green zone at €0.50 per 15 minutes with a four-hour maximum, with a €28 post-parking charge for overstaying [8]. After consultation the council adjusted the plan so that about 700 spaces went into the orange zone and nearly 3,500 into the green zone, and made the annual resident subscription sliding by family income and vehicle [6]. Free parking for electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles ended on 1 January 2023. The council cited 1,503 such vehicles registered on-street and 1,516 in car parks, which no longer allowed turnover [3].

Politics may change this. Olivier Falorni was elected mayor on 22 March 2026 [17] after making a free first half-hour of on-street parking his first campaign pledge [18]. In September 2026 he said it would be done within the 2027 budget, so it is not yet in force [19].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The city runs its parking itself. A city presentation of April 2023 says it chose to keep regulated parking in-house rather than use a private company, with 14 street wardens and two operating accounts, and lists a network including underground Verdun (570 spaces), Vieux Port Sud (615), Encan (420) and Vieux Port Ouest (410) [9]. We have not confirmed that this still holds in 2026. The reform leaflet announced two new car parks, Les Salines with 1,105 spaces near the former exhibition centre and Moitessier at the end of the Encan, to be put into service in early 2024 [7]. The Encan 2 car park scans number plates at entry and is paid by typing the plate number [11]. According to a June 2024 flyer, at Encan the first hour is free from 1 October to 30 June and 30 minutes free from July to September [12].

Park-and-ride is free. An August 2024 leaflet lists five sites in the agglomeration, with 20 to 300 spaces, and a €5 day pass for up to five people per car. The nearer Jean Moulin and Les Salines car parks are free for Yélo subscribers on the day of entry [13]. A free electric centre shuttle, financed by the city from unpaid-parking revenue, ran every 15 minutes from 4 July to 30 August 2026 [20]. Since 31 March 2026 on-street payment has run through the EasyPark app in place of Flowbird, and La Rochelle users pay no extra fee on the basic offer if they choose the city [15]. EV charging has been paid since February 2023, by energy delivered, with a two-hour maximum [16]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
All ten car parks in our La Rochelle data, 3,108 spaces, are listed under the city, with Jean Moulin shared with the Yélo transport network. Two are within 500 m of the Vieux-Port (1,030 spaces) and seven more within 1 km (1,907). The tenth is the automated motorhome area at Port-Neuf (171), which is further out. Our price data show €1.60 an hour in the main car parks, and a €14.55 day rate for motorhomes.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 53% on weekdays and 61% at weekends. The fullest are the small Cacaud car park (78%, 70 spaces) and Jean Moulin (76%, 450 spaces), followed by the motorhome area (65%) and Verdun's surface lot (60%). The largest, Verdun, is at 56% on weekdays and 63% at weekends. The Vieux-Port Ouest car park rises from 48% on weekdays to 71% at weekends, and Encan 1 from 33% to 50%. The emptiest are Encan 1 and 2 (33% and 28% on weekdays). Capacities in our feed differ slightly from the city's 2023 list, for example Encan at 420 against 416 and Vieux-Port Ouest at 420 against 410. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for La Rochelle.
